conviction_note: Findings sum to +1.6: a modest long lean from a three-quarter revenue-beat streak, a 26.2%-vs-21-23% margin beat last quarter, a strong counterparty enterprise-server print (Lenovo E&SMB infra +200% y/y) and a 22% sector-driven de-rating since 23 Oct, offset by a guided-in shift to future-start-date deals (the exact failure mode of the -17.75% Nov-2025 print) and persistent component shortages; abs_move 10.0 on the 9.98% event-implied move, p_up 54 because nothing here is a company number the market has not seen, so the scaled number is +0.8 and is smaller than the findings sum by design.
bar: Q1 FY27 revenue: company guide $755-765M (midpoint $760M) per the Q4 FY26 release (https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/26/nutanix-tops-estimates-as-external-storage-growth-helps-counter-hardware-squeeze/); consensus ~$762M from two agreeing sources (Earnings Whispers $761.8M, https://finviz.com/news/423404/nutanix-must-prove-its-beat-and-raise-turn-can-survive-persistent-server-shortages, 2026-11-16; Benzinga $761.9M, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NTNX/earnings-forecasts). Non-GAAP EPS bar is DISPUTED: $0.60 (Earnings Whispers) vs $0.53-0.54 (Benzinga / others) vs $0.61 (Investing.com); whisper $0.71. Non-GAAP op margin guide 26-28%. FY27 guide $3.18-3.23B revenue, 24-25% op margin, FCF $850-950M. EPS-dependent findings capped small because that bar is disputed.
positioning_check: Short interest about 12.0M shares, about 6.0 days to cover, up about 548K shares from the prior settlement (Equibles, settlement around 2026-11-13, https://equibles.com/stocks/ntnx/shortinterest); a Sep-30 figure on massive.com reads 11.93M and 4.6 days. That is roughly 4-5% of float: not a crowded short. Baseline: 25-delta skew +2.94 vol points (mild downside paid), put/call OI 0.73, ATM IV 69.1%, event-implied move 9.98%, 20d run-up -23.93%, 5d -2.11%, 25.9% off the 52w high ($75.98 on 2026-10-12). The drawdown coincides with a broad mid-November AI/tech selloff (Nasdaq -2.5% on 2026-11-16, SOX -5.3%) with no company-specific news found.

findings.finding: Nutanix has beaten revenue consensus in each of the last three quarters by about 2.4-2.5% (Q4 FY26: $757.1M vs $738.3M consensus, above its own guide; Q3 FY26 beat by 2.4%), while the Q1 FY27 consensus of ~$762M sits only $2M above the $760M guide midpoint, so a repeat of the streak would print ~$775-780M, above the top of the $755-765M range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the three beat-and-hold quarters of 2026 the stock rose +3.98% (Feb), +4.81% (May) and +6.81% (Aug); the one revenue miss with a weak outlook (Nov-2025) fell -17.75%. Beats have been paid on this name, not sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $762M sits inside the guide range, i.e. the Street has not extrapolated the beat cadence; if it had, the published consensus would sit near or above $765M and the whisper gap would be on revenue, not only on EPS ($0.71 vs $0.60). Partly priced: a beat is the base case for a habitual beater.
findings.independence: Q4 FY26 beat confirmed by SiliconAngle's results coverage (https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/26/nutanix-tops-estimates-as-external-storage-growth-helps-counter-hardware-squeeze/); the Q3 2.4% beat figure comes from Investing.com's 2026-08-26 preview (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/nutanix-earnings-up-next-with-focus-on-vmware-wins-fy27-outlook-93CH-4877361). Track record only, not a Q1 number.

findings.finding: Management said on the Q4 FY26 call it would use more future-start-date (FSD) contracts in FY27 to align license start with delayed server deliveries, and that a larger share of orders would start in future periods; this pushes recognized revenue out of the quarter in which ACV is booked — the same mechanism behind the Nov-2025 Q1 revenue and outlook miss that cost -17.75%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov-2025 (Q1 FY26): revenue and Q2 outlook fell short as analysts 'mulled a shift in revenue timing' — stock -17.75% (https://seekingalpha.com/news/4526239-nutanix-slumps-after-q1-revenue-outlook-miss-as-analysts-mull-shift-in-revenue-timing). Two later guidance cuts in FY26 were tied to server shortages and delayed start dates per Earnings Whispers.
findings.why_not_priced: The company says the FY27 guide already accounts for a higher FSD mix (William Blair via Blocks and Files), so this lands largely inside the guide; what is not priced is whether the Q2 guide and FY reiteration absorb it. If the market feared a repeat, skew would be well above +2.94 and the event-implied move above 10%.
findings.independence: Blocks and Files 2026-08-27 (https://www.blocksandfiles.com/hci/2026/08/27/nutanix-grows-despite-hardware-price-rises/5292962) quotes William Blair's Ader on 'a higher mix of future-start-date deals' built into the guide. Same call, so one fact.

findings.finding: Lenovo, a direct Nutanix hardware partner, reported on 2026-11-19 (quarter to 30 Sep, overlapping two-thirds of Nutanix's Aug-Oct quarter) Enterprise & SMB infrastructure revenue up 200% y/y and ISG revenue $11.3B (+178%), so enterprise servers were shipping in volume during the quarter, cutting against the thesis that server scarcity is stalling the on-prem projects Nutanix licenses ride on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior case of this stock reacting to a partner's server print; Nutanix's own FY26 guide cuts were blamed on server availability, so the line matters to the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Lenovo reported after Nutanix last spoke and is Hong Kong-listed, outside the US software tape; NTNX fell during the week of the print with the AI/tech selloff rather than reacting. Proxy only: dollar growth is inflated by memory prices and AI mix, and Lenovo also said DRAM/NAND shortages last through next year.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a Nutanix number. Supermicro's 2026-11-03 print (filed separately below) points the other way on supply.

findings.finding: Supermicro's CEO said on 2026-11-03 that 'key component shortage continue to impact delivery time line across the IT industry, even GPU', and Lenovo flagged DRAM/NAND shortages through next year; Nutanix itself guided that CPU/memory shortages and higher server prices last through all of FY27, so hardware-gated deal timing remains a live risk to the Q2 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26 guide cuts on server shortages preceded the -17.75% (Nov-2025) and -5.09% (Aug-2025) reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Nutanix already guided for persistent shortages. What would remain unpriced is a worsening vs the August assumption; nothing found shows that. Snippet-level quote via search summary.
findings.independence: Lenovo memory comment (https://en.jiemian.com/article/13662961.html) points the same way on supply; cuts against the Lenovo demand finding above, which is why both are small.

findings.finding: NTNX is down 22% from $70.58 (close 2026-10-23, per the Guggenheim initiation note) to $55.33 and 27% from its $75.98 high of 2026-10-12, with no company-specific news found; the moves coincide with sector selloffs (IGV -3% on 2026-10-16, Nasdaq -2.5%/SOX -5.3% on 2026-11-16), so the stock enters the print de-rated versus the August setup when it rallied 43% into the Q4 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into the Aug-2026 print the stock had run +43% since late May and still rose +6.81%; into Nov-2025 it was not de-rated and fell -17.75%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference: a sector-driven de-rating lowers the bar for a merely in-line guide. The skew (+2.94, mild) and implied move (9.98%) show the option market does not see this as a heavily one-sided setup.
findings.independence: Market context: https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/11/16/breaking-news/wall-street-tumbles-as-ai-jitters-hit-tech-stocks/ (2026-11-16); price $70.58 on 2026-10-23 from https://stock3.com/news/nutanix-guggenheim-setzt-auf-den-profiteur-des-vmware-frusts-17351548. Absence of company news is not itself evidence.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 non-GAAP operating margin was 26.2% against a 21-23% guide, and the ~5% workforce reduction (8-K of 2026-08-04, $33-43M charges) was to be substantially complete by end of October, inside Q1, so Q1 non-GAAP margin and EPS have room above the 26-28% guide; the EPS bar is disputed ($0.53 to $0.61), so this is capped small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beat 31% the quarter before Q4 and 22% in Q4 ($0.60 vs $0.49); stock rose in both. Management says savings are reinvested in go-to-market, so the margin beat is not a guide raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Whisper of $0.71 against $0.60 published shows the margin beat is largely expected; the residual is the size. If fully priced the stock would not be at the bottom of its post-earnings range.
findings.independence: Q4 margin vs guide from Earnings Whispers via finviz (2026-11-16); reinvestment plan from Blocks and Files (2026-08-27).

findings.finding: VMware-migration demand signals stayed positive into the quarter: Guggenheim initiated at Buy/$100 on 2026-10-26 calling Nutanix 'the only viable enterprise-wide replacement for VMware', KeyBanc noted vSphere 8 perpetual support ends October 2027 (forcing decisions), and UBS partner checks in August showed 40-50% y/y pipeline growth; these point to bookings/ARR (ARR $2.55B, +16% in Q4) holding up, though analyst notes are wire copy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ARR re-acceleration to 16% accompanied the +6.81% Aug-2026 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: these are published sell-side views. The stock has fallen 22% since the Guggenheim note, so the market is not paying for the migration story now; the residual is whether ARR/bookings confirm it.
findings.independence: KeyBanc and UBS from Investing.com 2026-08-26 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/nutanix-earnings-up-next-with-focus-on-vmware-wins-fy27-outlook-93CH-4877361); different notes, same theme.

findings.finding: Net revenue retention fell from 109% to 106% over the past year and management expects the FY27 renewals ACV cohort to grow more slowly, a structural drag on the recurring line that is already in the FY27 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NRR at 106% was reported alongside the +6.81% Aug-2026 reaction; it has not driven a reaction on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the guide and public; residual risk only if NRR slips below 106%.
findings.independence: Renewal cohort comment also in Blocks and Files 2026-08-27 (William Blair). Same call.

findings.finding: Insiders sold about $57.2M in the 12 months to 2026-10-26 with no open-market buys, including a sale on 2026-10-12 at $74.93-75.88 near the 52-week high; 87% was under 10b5-1 plans.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed link between insider sales and this stock's print reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly planned sales, public on EDGAR; minimal information.

outside_window.finding: Everpure (Pure Storage) fiscal Q3 results, the external-storage partner whose joint FlashArray+AHV offering feeds Nutanix external-storage bookings, report around early December, after the exit window.
KeyBanc: VMware vSphere 8 perpetual support ends October 2027, a forcing date for migration decisions that plays out over FY27-28, not this window.

baseline_tension: The mild long lean runs against the +2.94 put skew and the -24% 20-day run-up, but the skew is small and the drawdown is sector-driven rather than company-specific, so p_up is held near 50 (54) rather than leaning harder.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): FSD-mix finding moved -1.0 to -0.6 and NRR -0.3 to -0.2, because the company says both are already in the FY27 guide.

Rule 6 (disputed bar): the EPS/margin finding was capped from +0.5 to +0.3 because EPS consensus ranges $0.53-0.61 across sources; the revenue bar (guide plus two agreeing sources at ~$762M) left the beat-streak finding at +1.0.
Rule 5 (proxies smaller): Lenovo demand proxy +0.8 to +0.6, Supermicro supply proxy -0.5 to -0.4.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is not evidence): de-rating/positioning finding +0.8 to +0.5; kept because NTNX is a large cap and the drawdown has a sourced sector cause, but it is inference.
Wire copy is priced: the VMware analyst-notes finding moved +0.7 to +0.5; insider 10b5-1 selling -0.2 to -0.1.
Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 9.5 to 10.0, in line with the 9.98% event-implied move, since a Q2 guide and FY27 reiteration are due; p_up left at 54.
